patch.value:
Native close can unblock multiple dependents. At source `862dcee`, an ordinary error at `committing` starts their reverse restoration. A real process killed after the first dependent restore leaves the SDK journal without per-member progress. Retry mistakes its own history advance for a peer and leaves mixed lifecycle state.

PR #24 now delegates only fresh native closes. Interrupted or previously closed work returns `swarm_close_recovery_unsupported` without automatic primary or dependent restoration. [Issue 34](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/issues/34) and the related Feature own the full durable recovery protocol; this issue remains its narrower member-progress subtask.

Required design and acceptance:

- Persist a unique compensation identity, full member list, exact pre-close byte digests and post-close SDK history heads before the first restore.
- Bind native restore entries to that identity, member and exact restore target; never accept an unrelated copied message as ownership proof.
- Persist and fsync member progress and parent-directory changes; keep one owner of the SDK journal rather than racing its in-memory coordinator.
- Recovery skips certified restores, continues pending members and refuses peer edits with `swarm_compensation_partial`, preserving every foreign byte and audit entry.
- Run a real-process SIGKILL matrix after every restore boundary 0..N with 1–3 dependents. All members must reach exact pre-close item bytes, with append-only history. Inject a peer between restores and retain copied-marker regressions.
- Exercise packed npm/Bun consumers, document the protocol and prove regressions fail on revert.

Tracked by [pm-swarm-durable-compensation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/main/.agents/pm/issues/pm-swarm-durable-compensation.toon), split from [pm-swarm-y972](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-swarm-y972.toon).
Resume native close compensation after a process crash
